title: How Much Does LinkedIn Premium Cost? 2026 Plans
summary: LinkedIn premium cost varies by plan: Career at $39.99/month, Business at $69.99, and Sales Navigator at $119.99. Compare to find the best fit.
body_markdown:
## Fix manual lead handoff from LinkedIn with Activepieces


If the work you can name is retyping contacts, that's a handoff problem, and Activepieces fixes the handoff, not the subscription.


It chains steps together across 747 integrations, counted from its open source monorepo, and it starts working once a lead is already in a system you control.


Built to categorize HubSpot support tickets, the workflow below fires a HubSpot trigger on each new ticket, two AI steps rewrite and categorize it, a router splits it into branches with an "Otherwise" fallback, and three steps send messages to Slack, which means every new support ticket is automatically sorted and routed without manual intervention.


Swap the ticket for a lead and the structure holds: a contact lands in the CRM (customer database), the AI steps tidy the notes and tag the lead, the router assigns an owner, and Slack tells that person.


Renewal reminders for your own subscription follow the same trigger-and-notify pattern.


Activepieces' published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, so that router, those two AI steps and three Slack messages cost the same single credit (AI steps are the exception, priced higher), and the free plan carries 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's pricing page per module, so the same flow costs more on each of them with every step you add.


What it can't do is reach into LinkedIn and pull profiles out. LinkedIn's User Agreement prohibits bots and scrapers that automate activity on the site, so build only from the point where a lead is saved or entered by a person.


Check what your plan syncs to a CRM before you build anything.


If Sales Navigator already pushes saved leads into your CRM, let it, and use Activepieces for what happens next: routing, reminders, alerts, which fit inside the Plus plan at $20 a month flat with 10,000 credits.


If your plan lacks that sync, you're paying for lead tools and still funding a manual step.


On a shared agency login, that step is also where one client's lead volume quietly gets absorbed by the account holder's hours.


### Third-party LinkedIn contact-data tools and risks


The common shortcut is browser extensions that harvest contact details from profiles, and they sit on the wrong side of the same automation rule.


The risk lands on the account that runs them, which means a restricted login can stall every client on a shared seat.


A data provider with its own API, connected to Activepieces, where roughly 60% of the integrations are community-contributed, keeps the automation off LinkedIn entirely. You still pay that provider, so put its fee on the client's invoice rather than absorbing it.


If you save only a handful of leads in a week, pasting them into a sheet by hand costs less than building and maintaining a workflow. Automation pays back when the same copy-paste repeats daily across several people.


Below that, the free tier plus a shared spreadsheet is the honest answer, and no flow builder changes that.
